meals.name: Hearty Oatmeal with Banana and Nuts
instructions: Combine oats and water/milk in a saucepan.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until oats are creamy.
Pour into a bowl and top with sliced banana, chopped nuts, and cinnamon.
tips: For extra protein, stir in a spoonful of peanut butter.
Can be made with water to save on cost.

meals.name: Budget-Friendly Lentil Soup with Whole Grain Bread
ingredients: 1 cup dried brown or green lentils, rinsed
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add onion, carrots, and celery; cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant.
Add rinsed lentils, diced tomatoes, vegetable broth, and thyme. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 25-30 minutes, or until lentils are tender.
Season with salt and pepper. Serve hot with whole grain bread.
tips: Make a larger batch for easy leftovers throughout the week.
Add a pinch of red pepper flakes for a subtle kick.

meals.name: Quick Chicken & Veggie Stir-fry with Brown Rice
ingredients: 4 oz chicken breast, cut into strips
2 cups frozen mixed vegetables (broccoli, carrots, snap peas)
instructions: Cook brown rice according to package directions.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat.
Add chicken strips and cook until browned and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes. Remove chicken and set aside.
Add frozen mixed vegetables and minced garlic to the skillet and stir-fry for 5-7 minutes until tender-crisp.
Return chicken to the skillet. Stir in soy sauce and sesame oil. Toss to coat.
Serve hot over brown rice.
tips: Prep extra rice to use for other meals.
Add a dash of sriracha for a spicy kick.

meals.name: Scrambled Eggs with Whole Wheat Toast and Spinach
instructions: Heat olive oil in a non-stick skillet over medium heat.
Add spinach and cook until wilted, about 2-3 minutes. Remove from pan and set aside.
Whisk eggs with a pinch of salt and pepper.
Pour eggs into the skillet and scramble until cooked through.
Serve eggs with toast and wilted spinach.
tips: Add a slice of avocado for healthy fats if budget allows.
A sprinkle of cheese can add flavor.

meals.name: Black Bean & Corn Salad with Quinoa
ingredients: 1 can (15 oz) black beans, rinsed and drained
instructions: In a large bowl, combine cooked quinoa, black beans, corn, red bell pepper, and red onion.
In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, lime juice, salt, and pepper.
Pour dressing over the salad ingredients and toss to combine.
Stir in chopped cilantro if desired. Serve chilled or at room temperature.
tips: Prepare a larger batch of quinoa at the beginning of the week.
Add some diced avocado for extra creaminess if budget permits.

meals.name: Spaghetti with Marinara Sauce and Ground Turkey
instructions: Cook spaghetti according to package directions.
Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add ground turkey and cook, breaking it up with a spoon, until browned. Drain any excess fat.
Add chopped onion and minced garlic to the skillet with the turkey; cook until onion softens, about 5 minutes.
Stir in marinara sauce and bring to a simmer. Cook for 10-15 minutes.
Serve the sauce over cooked spaghetti.
tips: Add some frozen mixed vegetables to the sauce for extra nutrients.
Use whole wheat spaghetti for more fiber.

meals.name: Peanut Butter Banana Smoothie
instructions: Combine banana, milk, peanut butter, and ice cubes (if using) in a blender.
Blend until smooth and creamy.
Pour into a glass and serve immediately.
tips: Use frozen banana for a colder, thicker smoothie.
Add a handful of spinach for hidden greens.

meals.name: Tuna Salad Sandwich on Whole Wheat with Carrots
ingredients: 1 can (5 oz) tuna in water, drained
instructions: In a bowl, flake the drained tuna.
Add mayonnaise (or Greek yogurt), chopped celery, and onion (if using). Mix well.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Spread tuna salad onto one slice of whole wheat bread, top with lettuce, and then the other slice of bread.
Serve with carrot sticks on the side.
tips: Use Greek yogurt instead of mayonnaise for a lighter, higher protein option.
Add pickles or relish for extra flavor.

meals.name: Chicken & Broccoli Pasta
ingredients: 1.5 cups cooked whole wheat pasta (e.g., penne or rotini)
2 tbsp grated Parmesan cheese (optional, adds cost)
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Cook pasta according to package directions. Add broccoli florets to the pasta water during the last 3-4 minutes of cooking.
Drain pasta and broccoli, reserving 1/4 cup of pasta water.
While pasta cooks, heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add diced chicken and cook until browned and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes. Remove chicken and set aside.
Add minced garlic to the skillet and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return chicken to the skillet, add the drained pasta and broccoli.
Pour in chicken broth and reserved pasta water. Toss gently to combine.
Season with salt and pepper. Serve hot, topped with Parmesan cheese if desired.
tips: Use frozen broccoli to save on prep time.
A squeeze of lemon juice brightens the flavors.

meals.name: Oatmeal with Frozen Berries and Chia Seeds
ingredients: Drizzle of honey or maple syrup (optional)
instructions: Combine oats and water/milk in a saucepan. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until oats are creamy.
Stir in frozen berries and chia seeds. Cook for another minute until berries are slightly softened.
Pour into a bowl and drizzle with honey or maple syrup if desired.
tips: Chia seeds add omega-3s and fiber. You can use flax seeds instead.
Cook oats overnight for a quicker morning meal.

meals.name: Hummus & Veggie Wrap with Apple
ingredients: 1 large whole wheat tortilla or wrap
instructions: Lay the tortilla flat.
Spread hummus evenly over the tortilla, leaving a border around the edges.
Arrange the mixed greens, cucumber, and bell pepper over the hummus.
Roll up the tortilla tightly. Cut in half if desired.
Serve with a whole apple on the side.
tips: Add a sprinkle of feta cheese if you like.
This wrap is great for meal prepping and taking to work.

meals.name: Large Baked Potato with Chili (Bean-based)
ingredients: 1.5 cups homemade or canned bean chili (vegetarian or with minimal meat for budget)
2 tbsp plain Greek yogurt or sour cream (optional, adds cost)
1/4 cup shredded cheddar cheese (optional, adds cost)
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C). Wash the potato thoroughly and prick several times with a fork.
Bake directly on the oven rack for 50-60 minutes, or until fork-tender.
While potato bakes, gently heat chili in a saucepan.
Once potato is cooked, carefully slice it lengthwise and fluff the inside with a fork.
Top with warm chili. Add Greek yogurt/sour cream, cheese, and chives if desired.
tips: Make a big batch of bean chili on the weekend for easy weekday meals.
Microwave the potato for faster cooking (approx. 8-10 mins).
